rv.q: Not only does he get away with such a sentiment but there's an equivalent effect from hearing the night's best songs. A revelation.

RENT transferred to Broadway, where it won multiple Tony Awards, ran for 12 years and, when it closed, was the seventh longest-running show in Broadway history. It’s soon returning to the West End for a major anniversary revival.

The show which says and does exactly what it says on the tin and serves as a reminder of what we lost when 35 year old Larson, the composer of the dazzling musical RENT, died tragically in the early hours of the very day his magnum opus was due to open in New York, 30 years ago.
The Jonathan Larson Project is a must for fans of his work – both fascinating and slightly melancholy.
There are songs here I would love to hear again, and understanding how Larson progressed as an artist was enjoyable and instructive.

cn.t: Critics praise this heartfelt tribute to the Rent composer, celebrating lesser-known songs full of humor and emotion. Standout performances, particularly from Kassanga and Warren-Green, bring Larson's industrious songwriting legacy to glorious life.
